stories.title: Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey over Iranian threat
new_facts: Iran knew details of Trump's Turkey stay; threat involved a shoulder-fired missile.
Trump publicly confirmed the plane switch Tuesday, attributing it to Secret Service and military advice.
Rubio, Bessent, and Stephen Miller were among officials who traveled on the decoy Air Force One without Trump.
Democrats have formally called for a congressional briefing on the decoy operation.
Michael Wolff believes Trump himself leaked the secret plane switch story to the Washington Post.
White House journalists are outraged they were used as unknowing decoys without being warned of threat to their lives.
stories.line: Trump secretly switched planes in Turkey after Iran learned details of his NATO summit attendance, triggering protective measures.

stories.title: Paramount CEO threatens California exit over merger delays
new_facts: Paramount lawyer says company happy to cooperate; Democrats readying aggressive oversight of Paramount-Skydance/WBD merger.
Ellison told Paramount executives he is considering pulling company out of California amid multi-state AG lawsuit.
AG Bonta says Paramount is eager to settle; Bonta has had private conversations with Newsom about the case.
stories.line: A Paramount executive signals possible relocation amid state-level obstacles to merging with Warner Bros.

stories.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile as South Korea reports mixed job growth
new_facts: North Korea fired a ballistic missile ahead of S. Korea-U.S. military drills.
Missile flew more than 700 km, per South Korean military.
Japan's Defense Ministry independently confirmed a possible ballistic missile launch.
Launch originated from the Wonsan area, per South Korean military.
stories.line: North Korea launched a ballistic missile over 700 km; South Korea called it a provocation and reported job gains elsewhere remain uneven.

stories.title: South Carolina GOP primary heads to runoff for Graham's Senate seat
new_facts: Ralph Norman and Darline Graham advance to South Carolina GOP Senate runoff.
CBS News projects Graham and Norman advance to runoff for SC GOP Senate nomination.
With 84% counted: Graham 32.6%, Norman 24%, Fry 20.3%; Trump-backed Graham failed to secure outright win.
Darline Graham on-record denies nepo label, says she was not handed the seat.
stories.line: South Carolina Republicans advance two candidates to a runoff to replace Lindsey Graham's Senate seat.
